payload.name: Preserve distinct events on memory update
payload.description: When updating an existing memory, if the new evidence describes a different event time or different event than the stored memory, do not overwrite it; ADD a new memory instead.
content: Before performing UPDATE, check the retrieved existing memory against the incoming evidence: compare world_start/date, outcome, and key event facts.

If the incoming evidence refers to a different time or a different event instance even when the subject or topic is the same, do not UPDATE the existing memory. Create a new memory with ADD and leave the original memory unchanged.

When an existing memory records a completed event with a specific date, preserve that completion and date. A later related event must not replace those facts; if related, add a separate memory or use MERGE only when the facts describe the same event.

solves: An UPDATE overwrote a correctly stored past event with a later same-topic event, losing the original date and completion. The reusable mechanism is conflating distinct events that share a subject/topic. The rule is to compare event time and identity before updating; if they differ, ADD a new memory instead of overwriting. This applies whenever incoming evidence resembles an existing memory but describes a different time or different event.
